newsitem.title: FRANCE: European Commission should shrink - EU's Brittan.
newsitem.headline: European Commission should shrink - EU's Brittan.

text.p: The 20-member collegiate leadership of the European Commission is overweight and should be shrunk to a hard core of 10 commissioners with 10 more on a rotating basis from smaller EU states, European Commissioner Leon Brittan said on Thursday.

Brittan, in charge of trade at the European Commission in Brussels, said large EU countries which are currently allowed to nominate two members should be limited to one and the remaining places would be turned over between smaller countries.
"The Commission is too big and two members," Brittan told his audience at a European forum.
What was needed was a "hard core of 10", he said, with the smaller countries sharing the remaining posts on a rotating basis.

The issue is one of many being discussed under the auspices of the EU's inter-governmental conference on institutional reform as the EU plans to embrace Eastern Europe and further across the Mediterranean.
Brittan said the EU's Council of Ministers should be allowed to take more decisions by qualified majority, where it is now in some cases obliged to secure agreement by unanimity.

France in particular, but Germany too, have said they want the Commission shrunk. Britain has said it could swallow the idea but small countries like Ireland and Luxembourg have vehemently opposed the idea.
